clue.text: Rivals in union: one French — righteous, utterly — facing Scotsman linked to church

parts.note: un is French for one
holy means righteous, saintly
all, as in 'all alone', means utterly
Ian is a typically Scottish first name
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A sentence about a Frenchman of complete virtue standing beside a Scot who has ties to the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' and 'linked to' only join the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a pact between parties normally opposed, so former rivals joined together.

clue.text: Make psycho release the door?

definitions.meaning: to drive someone mad or unbalance their mind
literally, take a door off its hinges

explanation.surface: A puzzling instruction about a deranged person and a door.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange someone is to knock them off balance mentally, while freeing a door from its fittings is the literal sense.

clue.text: Excessive admiration of that man over rank or posting

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the next

parts.note: he refers to that man
a row or rank, as of soldiers or seats
shipping goods is posting or sending them

explanation.surface: A man's rank or job abroad is admired too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places HE above ROW in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolising someone is fawning reverence beyond what they deserve.

clue.text: Put clock up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a dial is a clock face; slang for a face too

explanation.surface: An instruction to hang a clock on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DIAL around in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of lay: something placed or set down has been put there.

clue.text: Attack while yacht maybe goes under

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece is placed under the first

parts.note: as can mean while, as in 'as I walked'
to yacht is one way to sail

explanation.surface: An assault launched as a boat sinks beneath the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes under' puts SAIL below AS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To assault or set upon someone vigorously, physically or with words.

clue.text: Book taxi home for cottage in wood?

parts.note: a log is a record book, as a ship's log
a cab is a taxi
in means at home

explanation.surface: Booking a cab to get home to a woodland cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple hut built from timber, so a cottage made of wood rather than among trees.

clue.text: Paint a toad for a change? Yes

definitions.text: Paint a toad for a change? Yes

indicators.note: the letters of the clue words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A whimsical suggestion to repaint an amphibian for variety, answered with approval.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: rearranging the letters is itself an alteration.
explanation.definitionFit: An alteration made to suit new conditions, so a change, which is exactly what reworking the letters is.

clue.text: Alludes to angry former employers?

parts.note: cross means angry
past employers supply job references, so they can be called references

explanation.surface: Someone mentions bosses from past jobs who are now furious.
explanation.definitionFit: To point a reader to another passage is to refer to it, a kind of mentioning.

clue.text: My being under doctor goes on

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits under the first

parts.note: my, used of oneself, is one's

explanation.surface: A patient complains of being under a doctor's care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' stands for the possessive of the impersonal pronoun, one's.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk on monotonously is to keep going on and on.

clue.text: That girl's gloves, we hear they've become separated

parts.note: her means that girl's

indicators.note: signals that the word is spoken and its sound is taken

parts.note: mitts are gloves

explanation.surface: Her mittens have come apart from each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Recluses live apart, cut off from society, so they have separated themselves.

clue.text: Thrill to have good racket after losing clubs

indicators.note: says the letter for clubs drops out of the noise word

parts.note: clamour is a loud racket
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A gambler is thrilled to have a good racket after a run of losses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link: G comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Allure and excitement: the thrill of glamour is its alluring, exciting charm.

clue.text: Having consumed whiskey, revolutionary number one is drunk, proverbially

indicators.note: says the turned-round number takes the whiskey letter inside it
turned round as in a revolution, so read backwards

parts.note: ten is a number
W is Whiskey in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A revolutionary leader downs whisky and becomes notoriously drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary number one' looks like a leader; 'one is drunk' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The British saying 'pissed as a newt' makes this amphibian the proverbial example of drunkenness.

clue.text: Wavering, abstain — RIP trying to please both sides?

indicators.note: unsteady, so the letters of the following words shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A politician who abstains is mocked as dead, trying to keep both parties happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Supported by or involving two opposing parties, so appealing to both sides.

clue.text: Latin period

parts.note: the Latin name for the era counted from the birth of Christ

explanation.surface: A stretch of time in Roman history.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'in the year of the Lord', naming the era since Christ's birth and, jokingly, old age.

clue.text: Go the wrong way with shopping trip?

parts.note: to err is to stray or go wrong
and means with, along with

explanation.surface: Getting lost on the way to the shops.
explanation.definitionFit: A short trip out to fetch something, such as groceries.

clue.text: Torture giving detectives bit of a shock

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors
a tress is a lock from a shock of hair

explanation.surface: Police detectives using electric shocks to torture someone.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'shock' of hair is a thick mass; 'giving' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe anguish or suffering, mental or physical, akin to torment.

clue.text: Redesigned atrium covering is sweet

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the next word
the letters of the room word are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A refitted entrance hall has a lovely new floor covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' looks like praise for the new look but names a dessert; 'Redesigned' gives TIRAMU, which 'covering' wraps round the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian dessert of coffee-soaked sponge and mascarpone, so a pudding or sweet.

clue.text: English welcome in patio after rambling about country

indicators.note: the greeting goes inside the scrambled letters
wandering about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: hi is a welcoming greeting

explanation.surface: An Englishman welcomed on a patio after a long ramble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is only a link here; 'rambling about' gives TOPIA, with the greeting set 'in' it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation in the Horn of Africa, capital Addis Ababa.

clue.text: Value of shares in players' organisation

definitions.meaning: the value of shareholders' stake in a company
the British trade union for actors goes by this name

explanation.surface: The share price of an actors' union.
explanation.definitionFit: Shareholders' stake in a firm carries this name, as does the British actors' union.

clue.text: Group in open red omnibus, backward-looking in fashion

indicators.note: the letters found are read from right to left
a group of letters sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A band rides on an open-top red bus, looking back at the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group in' picks NREDOM from 'open red omnibus' and 'backward-looking' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Current and up to date, so stylish and in vogue.

clue.text: Noun's disguised hiding place in puzzle

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold the abbreviation inside them
the letters wear a disguise, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A grammar puzzle where a noun is concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguised' gives NONUS; 'hiding' splits it after its third letter to take the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To baffle or perplex, used here as a verb.

clue.text: Forty per cent of public lose trust in Cabinet

indicators.note: six letters of the fifteen in the following words, two-fifths, are taken from inside them

explanation.surface: A poll shows four in ten people distrusting the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'public lose trust' has fifteen letters; the six hidden in it are forty per cent.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard is a closet, a storage cabinet.

clue.text: Lacking the capacity to host for five? Impossible to justify

indicators.note: the first word takes in the next pieces as guests

parts.note: unable means lacking the capacity
pro means for, in favour of
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A venue too small to host a dinner for five has no excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim that cannot be demonstrated cannot be justified.

clue.text: Chap touring Spain gets tight

indicators.note: going around the country's letter

parts.note: a chap is a man
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A man on holiday in Spain gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' looks like drunk; here it means stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight-fisted and miserly, unwilling to spend.

clue.text: Rent one's shed, sadly — that sounds different!

definitions.meaning: a rent is a rip in fabric

explanation.surface: Someone sadly gives up the rent on a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that sounds different' notes the two senses are pronounced differently, to rhyme with 'care' and 'fear'.
explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling covers both a rip in cloth and a drop from the eye.

clue.text: Is the Italian island phone firm turning over capital?

indicators.note: the assembled letters are flipped end to end

parts.note: taken as written
il is Italian for the
BT is British Telecom

explanation.surface: Asks whether an Italian island telephone company is boosting its turnover and capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Georgia.

clue.text: Outline device to have a lasting impression?

definitions.text: Outline device to have a lasting impression?

parts.words: Outline device to have a lasting impression?
parts.note: a cut-out sheet used to print a shape repeatedly

explanation.surface: A tool for drawing outlines that leaves a mark that lasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-out template through which paint or ink is applied to leave a design, a durable printed impression.

clue.text: Farming types with rustic guitars dancing around lake

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation
the letters move about as in a dance

explanation.surface: Country folk with rustic guitars dancing by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges RUSTIC GUITARS and 'around' puts L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: People who work the land are cultivators, farmers.
